This magic no knead bread recipe is so simple, requires very little hands on time and turns out the most incredible loaf of bread every single time. 

Mix together 3 cups of flour (plain, high grade, wholemeal - anything works here) ½ teaspoon of yeast, 1 teaspoon of salt and 1 ½ cups of warm water. Cover and leave it on the bench overnight or for at least 8 hours.

The next morning, heat a cast iron pot in the oven to 250°C while you shape the loaf. 

Tip the loaf onto the bench and shape it and if you have time, leave it to rest for 15 minutes or so and then shape it again.

Make a couple of scores on the top to let the steam escape and then bake it covered for 30 minutes at 220°C (reduce the oven temp as you put the bread in) and then uncovered for another 15 minutes until it’s golden brown and the crust has crisped up.

Slice it up and enjoy!

Sourdough Bread 🍞 Jalapeño Cheddar (Easy & Flavorful!)

For Dough:
280 g bread flour (or all purpose flour)
70 g whole wheat flour 
270 g water
70 g sourdough starter 
7 g salt 

For filling:
2 small fresh jalapeños 
50 g cheddar cheese 
- make a smooth paste from the jalapeños and cheddar using either a mortar and pestle or a blender

Fermentation Temperature 23-24°C (73–77.0°F)

1. Water + sourdough starter + flour. Mix. 1 hour rest.

2. Add Salt. 1 hour rest. 

3. Perform 3 sets of coil folds with 1-hour intervals. During the first coil fold, add inclusions (Jalapeño Cheddar Paste).

4. After the last fold, allow the dough to ferment for 1.5 - 2 hours.

5. Pre-shape the dough and let it rest for 20 minutes.

6. Shape the dough and place it in the fridge for an overnight cold retard.

7. The next day, score the bread.

8. Bake in a preheated oven at 250°C (482°F) about 20 minutes with steam (if using open baking) or with the lid on (if using a Dutch oven).

9. Remove the steam or take off the lid, then bake for another 15–20 minutes at 200°C (392°F) until golden brown.

But this clever idea uses something that normally has nothing to do with painting—a transparent umbrella.

The technique involves attaching an inverted transparent umbrella to the extension pole of the paint roller.

As the paint is applied to the ceiling, the umbrella acts as a protective barrier, catching droplets before they fall onto the surrounding area. This can help keep the workspace cleaner and reduce the amount of additional protection needed for furniture and floors.

The transparent material is an especially clever detail. It allows the painter to maintain a clear view of the ceiling while working, making it easier to keep the application precise.

The umbrella can also be used on the floor as a makeshift support for the paint tray or can, helping protect the surface from accidental spills.

Still, creativity shouldn’t replace proper safety precautions. When working at height, use a stable, appropriate ladder or other suitable equipment rather than improvised or unstable surfaces.

It’s a simple example of how an everyday object can be repurposed to make a messy household task more practical.

725g warm filtered water
250g active sourdough starter (eloise)
30g salt
1000g bread flour

-  mix ingredients together
-  let sit for one hour
-  perform 4 sets of stretch and folds or coil and folds every 30 mins for 2 hours
-  bulk ferment on counter for 4 hours
-  split dough into 2 loafs and roll into their balls, can add inclusions here
-  refrigerate for 2 hours or up to 4 days
-  when ready to bake, score and bake at 500 degrees with the lid on for 35 mins, then lower to 450 degrees and bake for 10 mins with the lid off (watching for color)

If you have never made bread before but want to try, this is the exact recipe you need to start with! 🍞

This magic no knead bread recipe is so simple, requires very little hands on time and turns out the most incredible loaf of bread every single time. 

Mix together 3 cups of flour (plain, high grade, wholemeal - anything works here) ½ teaspoon of yeast, 1 teaspoon of salt and 1 ½ cups of warm water. Cover and leave it on the bench overnight or for at least 8 hours.

The next morning, heat a cast iron pot in the oven to 250°C while you shape the loaf. 

Tip the loaf onto the bench and shape it and if you have time, leave it to rest for 15 minutes or so and then shape it again.

Make a couple of scores on the top to let the steam escape and then bake it covered for 30 minutes at 220°C (reduce the oven temp as you put the bread in) and then uncovered for another 15 minutes until it’s golden brown and the crust has crisped up.

Slice it up and enjoy!

Sourdough Bread 🍞 Jalapeño Cheddar (Easy & Flavorful!)

For Dough:
280 g bread flour (or all purpose flour)
70 g whole wheat flour 
270 g water
70 g sourdough starter 
7 g salt 

For filling:
2 small fresh jalapeños 
50 g cheddar cheese 
- make a smooth paste from the jalapeños and cheddar using either a mortar and pestle or a blender

Fermentation Temperature 23-24°C (73–77.0°F)

1. Water + sourdough starter + flour. Mix. 1 hour rest.

2. Add Salt. 1 hour rest. 

3. Perform 3 sets of coil folds with 1-hour intervals. During the first coil fold, add inclusions (Jalapeño Cheddar Paste).

4. After the last fold, allow the dough to ferment for 1.5 - 2 hours.

5. Pre-shape the dough and let it rest for 20 minutes.

6. Shape the dough and place it in the fridge for an overnight cold retard.

7. The next day, score the bread.

8. Bake in a preheated oven at 250°C (482°F) about 20 minutes with steam (if using open baking) or with the lid on (if using a Dutch oven).

9. Remove the steam or take off the lid, then bake for another 15–20 minutes at 200°C (392°F) until golden brown.

Painting a ceiling is often one of the most demanding parts of a renovation. Besides the physical effort, there’s another unavoidable problem: paint droplets landing on the floor, furniture, and even the person holding the roller.

But this clever idea uses something that normally has nothing to do with painting—a transparent umbrella.

The technique involves attaching an inverted transparent umbrella to the extension pole of the paint roller.

As the paint is applied to the ceiling, the umbrella acts as a protective barrier, catching droplets before they fall onto the surrounding area. This can help keep the workspace cleaner and reduce the amount of additional protection needed for furniture and floors.

The transparent material is an especially clever detail. It allows the painter to maintain a clear view of the ceiling while working, making it easier to keep the application precise.

The umbrella can also be used on the floor as a makeshift support for the paint tray or can, helping protect the surface from accidental spills.

Still, creativity shouldn’t replace proper safety precautions. When working at height, use a stable, appropriate ladder or other suitable equipment rather than improvised or unstable surfaces.

It’s a simple example of how an everyday object can be repurposed to make a messy household task more practical.
